race_context: Avon Community School Corporation serves Avon and Washington Township in Hendricks County; the district describes its 2018 operating referendum as approved by 'Avon-Washington Township voters' {acsc_ref}. It operates Avon High School, Avon Academy, Avon Online, three middle schools (North, South and West), eight elementary schools and White Oak Early Learning Center {acsc_appreciation}.

Superintendent Scott Wyndham told WISH-TV in August 2024 that the district opened that school year with 'just about 11,000 students,' its largest enrollment to that point {wish_2024}; a current-year official enrollment figure was not found in fetched sources.

The board has five members: Sarah Parent (president), Mike Langford (vice president), Jennifer Smith (secretary), Kim Woodward and Josh Yoder {acsc_board}{acsc_appreciation}. Yoder joined the board in January 2026, when the board also honored retiring member Cindy Simmons {acsc_appreciation}.

Two seats are on the 2026 ballot. The Hendricks County 2026 general ballot lists 'Avon School Board — Washington' with vote for 2 and two candidates, Sarah Parent and Jennifer Smith, both with no party selection {hc_ballot}; the state list's 'vote for 1' does not match the county ballot {in_list}{hc_ballot}. Both candidates are the sitting board members who joined the board in 2023 {acsc_board}, and GoodParty.org lists both of their current terms as 2022–2026 {goodparty_avon}. With two candidates for two seats, the race is uncontested {hc_ballot}.

Budget and taxes: Avon voters approved an operating referendum in May 2018 and renewed it in November 2025 at a maximum rate of $0.33; the district set the 2026 rate at $0.31 and says the money funds smaller class sizes, educator hiring and retention, and student supports such as elementary counselors and multilingual learner specialists {acsc_ref}. The district says 2025's SEA 1 'gives homeowners an additional 10% tax credit (up to $300) over and above 1% tax cap savings' {acsc_ref}.

2027 budget: at an August 2026 working session the board reviewed 2027 budget assumptions and cited property tax caps, insurance cost increases and legislative changes to school funding as challenges, according to a meeting summary; public commenters questioned legal spending compared with instructional funding {govly_aug2026}. A budget hearing was scheduled for Sept. 30 and adoption for Oct. 26, 2026 {govly_aug2026}{acsc_board}.

Facilities and growth: in 2024 the district was building a third middle school, expanding Avon High School and its existing middle schools, and redistricting grades K–8 for 2025–26, moving fifth grade into elementary schools and sixth grade into middle schools {wish_2024}. At the August 2026 session the board voted 5-0 to keep using design-build for its 2027 capital improvement project {govly_aug2026}.
No candidate forums or questionnaires for this race were found. Only Sarah Parent had posted a statement on the county's candidate biography page as of this review {hc_avon_bios}.
